title: Scaffolding and work above 2 metres in New South Wales
moduleTitle: Optional add-on: high-risk work and platform licences
audience: Workers and supervisors who may be asked to work at height or on a platform. Optional add-on, taken alongside the main courses.
learningOutcomes: Apply the NSW scaffold licence threshold of 4 metres.
Identify the SWMS trigger at 2 metres and the point that is not confirmed.

instruction.heading: Scaffold licence
instruction.body: SafeWork NSW's work at heights page says a scaffold licence is needed to erect, alter or dismantle a scaffold where the fall or falling-object risk is more than 4 metres (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Safe work method statement
instruction.body: The same page says a safe work method statement is needed where a person could fall more than 2 metres (no date shown).

instruction.heading: What is not confirmed
instruction.body: Whether the high-risk work licence rules apply to work over 2 metres is not confirmed by an official source. The page sets out the SWMS and fall-prevention duties at 2 metres, but it does not tie a high-risk licence rule to that height.

procedure: Measure the fall height and the falling-object risk.
Where the fall could exceed 2 metres, prepare a safe work method statement.
Where the fall or falling-object risk is more than 4 metres for scaffolding, check the scaffold licence rule before work.

workedExamples.situation: A crew in New South Wales must erect a scaffold where the fall or falling-object risk is about 5 metres.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which licence rule in this lesson applies?
workedExamples.reasoning: The scaffold licence threshold of more than 4 metres is stated on the SafeWork NSW page, so a licence is needed to erect the scaffold. This add-on grants no licence.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a high-risk rule starts at 2 metres.
commonErrors.prevention: The page states an SWMS trigger at 2 metres; the high-risk rule at that height is not confirmed.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A scaffold licence is required above the 4 metre risk threshold in New South Wales. This lesson does not grant that licence.

qualityStandard: Learner states the SWMS trigger and the scaffold licence threshold separately.
documentationEvidence: Fall height, falling-object risk and the SWMS reference recorded before work.
summary: NSW scaffold licence threshold: more than 4 metres of fall or falling-object risk.
SWMS trigger: more than 2 metres of fall.
High-risk rule at 2 metres is not confirmed.

knowledgeChecks.question: At what height does the NSW scaffold licence threshold in this lesson apply?
options: Where the fall or falling-object risk is more than 2 metres
Where the fall or falling-object risk is more than 4 metres
Where the scaffold is over 11 metres

officialReferences.title: Work safely at heights in construction (SafeWork NSW)
officialReferences.covers: SWMS needed where a person could fall more than 2 metres; scaffold licence where the fall or falling-object risk is more than 4 metres. Does not tie a high-risk rule to 2 metres.
